clips.text_zh: 十年long only淨係揸一樣，你揀BTC定係黃金？我兩邊都輸過，廢柴一個。真係要比，黃金我揸過實物，但Bitcoin真係我嘅信仰，又係信仰，唔知啦lol。
clips.text_en_b1: If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? The question asks what makes your choice better than the other. Bitcoin has rallied hard this cycle, but gold is hitting new highs too. Both seem to win, which is why this debate keeps going on /biz/.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking BTC vs gold 10-year hold

signal.rationale: Anecdotal debate post, no actionable setup

clips.text_en_b2: If you were forced to go long-only on a single asset over the coming decade, would you pin your bet on Bitcoin or gold? Both have posted remarkable gains this cycle, with BTC rallying aggressively while bullion keeps grinding out fresh highs. The whole debate keeps dragging on across /biz/ precisely because nobody can crown a clear winner. Personally, I've taken losses on both, so I'm hardly the one to judge — but having held physical gold myself, I'll admit Bitcoin borders on pure faith…
clips.text_en_c1: If one were compelled to hold a single asset over the coming decade, the perennial question resurfaces: Bitcoin or gold? This cycle has witnessed Bitcoin rallying with extraordinary force, yet gold has simultaneously notched successive all-time highs, which only intensifies the debate on /biz/. The framing presupposes that any choice must demonstrably outperform its alternative, a standard that both instruments arguably satisfy under prevailing macroeconomic conditions. Personally, I have held physical bullion and incurred losses on both, the eternal dilemma of conviction versus conviction, though Bitcoin remains, for want of a better word, an article of faith.
clips.text_en_c2: Were one compelled, by some hypothetical imperative, to select a single asset and hold it long-only across the coming decade, the perennial contest between Bitcoin and gold inevitably resurfaces, animated by devotees on either side who insist their conviction rests on something more substantial than mere sentiment. The contrarian case for either remains genuinely compelling: Bitcoin, the lodestar of a generation disenchanted with monetary orthodoxy, has rallied with ferocious velocity this cycle, while gold, that ancient store of value, has simultaneously scaled unprecedented nominal highs. To argue decisively that one constitutes the superior allocation betrays a certain naivety, yet if pressed, I would confess that Bitcoin constitutes something approaching an article of faith for me, an ideological commitment whose rational foundations I can no longer fully disentangle from sheer conviction.

clips.text_zh: SpaceX IPO lockup又有嘢爆。9月2026大約3.19億股解禁，大約7%個baseline pool。Elon條友一出貨，TSLA同SpaceX相關全部都震，我個CFD又輸，wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: On September 9, 2026, about 319 million extra SpaceX shares become eligible for sale. That is around 7 percent of the baseline pool, roughly 2.4 percent of total shares outstanding. This is the 90th trading day since the IPO and the third major lockup release event.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread tracking SpaceX IPO lockup schedule

signal.rationale: Not a trade, pure macro event note

clips.text_en_b2: Another SpaceX IPO lockup cliff just surfaced in filings. Come September 9, 2026, roughly 319 million additional shares become eligible for trading, which works out to about 7 percent of the baseline pool and roughly 2.4 percent of total shares outstanding. This marks the third major lockup release and the 90th trading day since the IPO. The moment Elon even hints at offloading, every TSLA and SpaceX-linked position trembles, and sure enough, my CFD bled out again.
clips.text_en_c1: Yet another SpaceX lockup expiry has detonated across trading desks. On 9 September 2026, approximately 319 million shares become eligible for sale, representing roughly seven percent of the baseline pool and around 2.4 percent of total shares outstanding. This constitutes the third major lockup release and the ninetieth trading day since the IPO, a milestone that historically precipitates pronounced volatility. Should Elon offload a meaningful tranche, the contagion would inevitably ripple through TSLA and adjacent equities. My CFD position, once again, absorbed the brunt of the cascade.
clips.text_en_c2: Another lockup expiry event has detonated across the SpaceX shareholder register, and the collateral damage, predictably enough, extends well beyond the immediate ticker. On or about September 9, 2026, an additional 319 million shares become eligible for sale, a tranche that, while representing a comparatively modest seven percent of the baseline pool, constitutes something closer to 2.4 percent of the total shares outstanding. This milestone marks the ninetieth trading day since the IPO and, crucially, the third significant lockup release since listing, each event functioning as a stress examination of market depth and holder conviction. The mere possibility that Elon might liquidate even a fraction of his position sends tremors through anything tangentially connected, whether directly via SpaceX equity or indirectly through Tesla's symbiotic exposure.

clips.text_zh: MIT有篇paper話AI會搞死民主。自動化和AI取代晒啲人工，財富集中曬去資本家，唔平等爆煲就會壓迫工人。AI連我呢啲surveyor assistant都搞掂埋啦，廢物。
clips.text_en_b1: A Nobel-winning MIT economist published a paper called Automation and Repression. It says that as AI and automation replace human labor, wealth concentrates heavily in the hands of a tiny group of capital owners. Inequality skyrockets. When it hits a critical mass, workers realize they are crushed and the threat of revolt spikes.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread discussing MIT paper on AI and inequality
clips.text_en_b2: A Nobel-winning MIT economist just dropped a paper titled Automation and Repression, arguing that as AI and automation steadily displace human labor, wealth piles up in the hands of a tiny elite. Once that inequality crosses a critical threshold, workers grasp how thoroughly they've been crushed, and the latent threat of revolt spikes sharply. The paper's grim forecast already feels uncomfortably close to home — even my own surveying assistant role is being automated away, which is frankly infuriating.
clips.text_en_c1: A Nobel-laureate economist from MIT has circulated a paper provocatively titled Automation and Repression, advancing the thesis that AI and automation will displace human labour so comprehensively that wealth accumulates in the hands of a vanishingly small capital-owning elite. Once inequality crosses a critical threshold, the dispossessed masses recognise their predicament, at which point the latent threat of insurrection spikes precipitously. The implications extend well beyond macroeconomic abstraction; even surveyor assistants, my own profession included, may find themselves redundant.
clips.text_en_c2: A paper emerging from MIT, authored by an economist whose credentials include the rather considerable distinction of a Nobel Prize, has articulated a thesis sufficiently bleak to warrant sustained attention. Titled Automation and Repression, the work advances the proposition that as artificial intelligence and automated systems progressively render human labor redundant, the resultant concentration of wealth among an ever-diminishing stratum of capital owners will accelerate inequality beyond any historical precedent. When this stratification reaches critical mass, the paper contends, the displaced workforce will arrive at an unmistakable recognition of its predicament, at which juncture the latent threat of popular revolt will intensify commensurately, prompting preemptive repressive measures from those who control the commanding heights of the economy.

clips.text_zh: 美國財長Bessent想串中國補貼，結果全世界淨係記住一句：「BYD係$70,000嘅車，$35,000買到」。2026年最佳免費廣告，外國人都識BYD，國產車真係起勢。
clips.text_en_b1: US official Bessent tried to slam China over EV subsidies and policy. He said BYD is the best $70,000 car that $35,000 can buy. People only heard the price line. It became the best free ad for BYD in 2026. The internet will not let you bury a product, only promote it.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread mocking US official's BYD comment
clips.text_en_b2: US official Bessent clearly intended to shame China over its EV subsidies and industrial policy, yet all the internet retained was a single devastating line: BYD is essentially a $70,000 car you can grab for $35,000. Rather than burying the brand, his comment backfired spectacularly and became the most valuable free advertisement BYD received in 2026. Foreign audiences worldwide now recognize the name, and honestly, domestic Chinese automakers are genuinely hitting their stride.
clips.text_en_c1: In a remarkable instance of political overreach, US official Bessent sought to criticise Chinese EV subsidies and industrial policy, inadvertently crafting what may stand as 2026's most consequential advertisement. His assertion that BYD constitutes a seventy-thousand-dollar vehicle obtainable for thirty-five thousand distilled precisely the value proposition the brand had struggled to articulate globally. The soundbite metastasised across social media; netizens retained only the price differential. The internet, it seems, refuses to bury products, it amplifies them, and foreign consumers now recognise BYD as never before.
clips.text_en_c2: In what must rank among the more exquisitely self-defeating interventions in recent diplomatic memory, US Treasury official Bessent evidently sought to chastise China over the particulars of EV subsidies and industrial policy, only to discover that the internet, with its remorseless appetite for quotable ammunition, has extracted from his remarks a single, immortal phrase. The line in question, asserting that BYD constitutes essentially the finest seventy-thousand-dollar vehicle obtainable for thirty-five thousand, has transmogrified into the most gratuitously effective advertisement the Chinese automaker could conceivably have hoped for in 2026. Whatever nuance Bessent intended has been comprehensively obliterated; what endures is the price comparison, repeated across every conceivable platform. The episode furnishes a near-perfect illustration of the contemporary attention economy's cardinal rule: the internet permits no product to be buried, only amplified.

clips.text_zh: 西人都係廢，開發商訂咗合理規則都唔遵守。LOL S15外卡選手成日犯規，好彩我淨係觀眾，唔使煩。
clips.text_en_b1: Why are Westerners unable to obey entirely reasonable rules from developers? The thread complains about Western gamers breaking basic in-game rules that East Asian players follow without thinking. Mods, devs, and entire communities seem to lose their minds when a rule is even mentioned.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread complaining about Western gamer behaviour
clips.text_en_b2: Why do Western gamers consistently fail to follow entirely reasonable rules that developers lay down? The thread laments how Western League of Legends players at the S15 international wild card bracket keep breaking basic in-game etiquette that East Asian competitors observe without a second thought. Moderators, developers, and entire subcommunities appear to lose their minds the moment anyone even dares to mention a rule. Meanwhile I'm just a spectator, so at least I don't have to deal with the fallout.
clips.text_en_c1: Why do Western gamers routinely flout the most elementary rules that developers, with considerable deliberation, have established? The thread laments a perceived cultural divergence whereby East Asian competitors observe standard protocols instinctively, whereas Western players appear constitutionally incapable of compliance. When moderators or developers merely reference the offending regulations, entire communities descend into paroxysms of indignation. The LOL S15 wildcard participants, in particular, seem constitutionally opposed to adherence, a phenomenon I observe with considerable relief from the comfortable remove of spectatorhood.
clips.text_en_c2: The capacity of Western gaming communities to flagrantly disregard rules that any reasonable observer would consider entirely uncontroversial constitutes one of the more confounding phenomena in contemporary multiplayer culture. The thread in question enumerates, with weary exasperation, how Western competitors in League of Legends' Season 15 wildcard circuit persistently violate foundational in-game protocols that their East Asian counterparts appear to internalize instinctively, as though the norms were encoded at some quasi-genetic level. What renders the spectacle particularly irksome is the disproportionate institutional response: moderators, developers, and entire community infrastructures appear to undergo collective apoplexy whenever the mere existence of a rule is invoked, transforming what should be a settled matter into an interminable procedural crisis.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信成日笑我只做bench唔練BJJ。「315lbs bench，摺你一半」佢咁講。佢50磅瘦過我都搞到我仆街，聽日去gym啦ok。
clips.text_en_b1: Hey, nice bench press, 315 pounds really impressive. Now I will fold you in half. You have no reason not to train grappling, unless you want a guy 50 pounds lighter than you to make you his bitch. Any half-decent grappler would have you staring at your own asshole in seconds.
clips.text_en_b2: Nice bench press, champ — 315 pounds, genuinely impressive. Now allow me to fold you in half without breaking a sweat. Honestly, there's no defensible excuse for skipping grappling training unless you're perfectly content letting some guy fifty pounds lighter than you turn you into his personal punching bag. Any halfway competent grappler would have you reassessing your entire athletic identity in about ten seconds flat. See you at the gym tomorrow, I suppose.
clips.text_en_c1: Congratulations on your 315-pound bench press; an undeniably respectable achievement, and one which I shall now proceed to dismantle entirely. Should you persist in neglecting grappling, any competitor a mere fifty pounds lighter will reduce you to a supine, contemplative position within seconds. The bench constitutes but one facet of combat athletics, and a half-competent Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu practitioner would have you examining your own posterior with minimal exertion. Training BJJ tomorrow is, by any rational calculus, the soundest available investment of your time.
clips.text_en_c2: Compliments regarding one's bench press, however graciously proffered, frequently function as little more than prelude to an unsolicited discourse on grappling, delivered with the evangelical certitude of the recently converted. The fat interlocutor in question, having registered my 315-pound lift with what I had naively interpreted as admiration, immediately pivoted to the observation that he would, in his professional estimation, fold me in half, a characterization whose anatomical specificity I found myself disinclined to verify empirically. The argument's central thesis was unassailable: absent dedicated grappling training, one remains vulnerable to domination by opponents substantially smaller, the cited disparity being a mere fifty pounds, a deficit that evidently confers negligible advantage when the contest migrates horizontal. Any competent practitioner, he assured me, would have me contemplating my own navel in embarrassingly short order.

clips.text_zh: 終於睇咗鏈鋸人漫畫Reze篇，雖然冇睇劇場版，但電影感好正。Season 1雖然畀人話，但panel layout本身就係cinematic，我又多一樣廢事。
clips.text_en_b1: Chainsaw Man volumes 6 and 7. I did not watch the Reze arc movie in theaters, but I always liked season 1, so I started reading the manga recently. I can see why everyone loved the movie. The manga is very enjoyable. People shit on the direction of season 1, but the cinematic style fits the panel layouts.
clips.text_en_b2: I finally got around to reading the Chainsaw Man Reze arc in volumes 6 and 7, having skipped the theatrical release entirely, though I'd genuinely enjoyed the first season back in the day. The manga absolutely lives up to the hype, and I can see precisely why audiences flocked to the film adaptation. While plenty of viewers criticized the direction of season 1, the cinematic flourishes actually suit the panel layouts remarkably well — so apparently I've acquired yet another obsessive hobby.
clips.text_en_c1: Having finally perused the Chainsaw Man Reze arc in its manga incarnation, volumes six and seven proved thoroughly rewarding despite my having bypassed the theatrical release. Season one attracted considerable criticism for its directorial choices, yet the source material's panel layouts lend themselves naturally to cinematic translation, a structural quality that renders the animated adaptation's stylistic decisions defensible upon reflection. The cinematic sensibility permeates every sequence, and one emerges appreciating how the static page anticipated the kinetic possibilities of film.
clips.text_en_c2: Having at long last acquainted myself with the Reze arc of Chainsaw Man, encompassing volumes six and seven, I find myself belatedly comprehending the fervor that surrounded its theatrical adaptation, a film I regrettably declined to witness in cinemas. My tardiness notwithstanding, the experience of encountering the material in its original sequential-art form proved thoroughly rewarding, the narrative possessing an unmistakable cinematic sensibility that transcends the conventional limitations of the medium. Season 1 of the anime, which attracted considerable critical opprobrium for its directorial choices, increasingly appears vindicated upon comparison with the source material, whose panel compositions themselves exhibit a distinctly filmic grammar.
